verdicts.quote: A CSV containing one otherwise valid new record and one invalid record creates neither account.
If a reported data-record error concerns a record starting on physical line 5, the error contains the number 5.

Submitting a record with an identity already present in the applicable scope reports a conflict for that record... Submitting two records with the same new identity reports a conflict within the file.
An admin cannot assign rights through import that ordinary user creation would prohibit that admin from assigning.
An admin with user-creation authority submits a CSV file through the product.
verdicts.missing: Whether bulk import is a distinct permission; the spec ties it to ordinary user-creation authority rather than stating it is not implied by it.

verdicts.quote: A file with user values as its first nonempty record and no header is rejected. ... A header containing an unrecognized field is rejected. ... Omitting that column fails the check.

Adding a UTF-8 byte order mark ... does not change the first field name ... LF or CRLF record endings have equivalent outcomes ... a quoted field containing a comma ... or a line break imports as one field
If a submission fails in a product that sends onboarding notifications on user creation, its proposed users receive no such notifications from that submission.
A file of 1,048,577 bytes fails it. ... A file with 1,001 user records below the byte ceiling fails that check. ... tells the admin the maximum for the exceeded measurement.
A zero-byte file, a file containing only empty lines, and a header-only file each fail with an outcome indicating the absence of user records. ... A valid one-record submission creates its user.
The admin resubmits a file whose accounts are all still present. No second account is created for any of those identities.
While any account creation in the submission is still pending, the admin sees no success outcome for that submission.
verdicts.missing: Whether large files are processed synchronously or in the background, and how the admin is told a background import finished.

verdicts.quote: the imported user receives the corresponding notification after the account is created.
verdicts.missing: Whether up to 1,000 notifications are sent at once and any pacing or throttling of them.

verdicts.quote: A newly imported user starts in the same initial account state as a comparable ordinarily created user, where the product defines that state.
verdicts.missing: Active vs pending, whether a password is set or supplied, and how the user first signs in when no host rule exists.

verdicts.quote: If ordinary user creation is required to produce an audit record, a reviewer can find the required audit information for a user created by import.
verdicts.missing: An import-level audit record of who imported which file and when, independent of existing per-user audit requirements.

verdicts.quote: an admin can still use it after import is introduced with the same permissions, inputs, and outcomes. ... accounts that existed before the submission retain their user data.
